humanities_role_explanation: Questions span general-knowledge topics (science & technology, politics, art, geography, sports, music, TV, history, video games); humanities topics such as art and history only supply content for generic short-form factual QA, and the competence tested is factuality, not disciplinary skill.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only short questions with short text answers.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Short, fact-seeking questions with a single indisputable answer (short-form factuality), graded correct/incorrect/not attempted. Calibration is measured via stated confidence and answer-frequency over 100 samples ('know what they know').

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-topic factual QA benchmark covering many domains, not scoped to one humanities domain.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3-haiku, Claude-3-sonnet, Claude-3-opus, Claude-3.5-sonnet, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1-preview.

quantitative_metrics.note: Correct, not attempted, incorrect, correct given attempted, F-score; calibration plots.

summary: SimpleQA is a benchmark of 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions with single indisputable answers, adversarially collected against GPT-4 responses. Models are graded correct/incorrect/not attempted by a prompted ChatGPT grader, and calibration is also measured.
key_findings: Frontier models score low: o1-preview best with 42.7% correct and F-score 44.8; GPT-4o 38.2% correct; Claude-3.5-sonnet 28.9% correct but F-score 35.0, as Claude models abstain more often. Larger models are better calibrated, but all overstate confidence.
facets_explanation: AI trainers (human annotators) wrote questions and reference answers with supporting web links, and a second independent trainer answered; only matching questions were kept, with two unique source domains required. Questions with multiple answers or ambiguity were removed or treated as errors (~3% estimated error rate). Questions are closed-book factual with one gold target graded by a prompted ChatGPT classifier.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports o1-preview with Correct 42.7, Not attempted 9.2, Incorrect 48.1, Correct given attempted 47.0, F-score 44.8; the headline is the 'Correct' percentage (treated as accuracy). GPT-4o scores 38.2 correct. The third-trainer check gave 94.4% agreement, but this is a data-quality check, not a human baseline on the same metric as the models.

humanities_role.quote: SimpleQA contains questions from a wide range of topics, including history, science & technology, art, geography, TV shows, etc.

dataset_size.quote: We present a benchmark called SimpleQA, which contains 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions.

gold_source.quote: First, AI trainers (i.e., human annotators) created question and answer pairs.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Here we only focus on objective knowledge and force questions to be written such that they only have a single, indisputable answer.

answer_multiplicity.quote: questions are created such that there exists only a single, indisputable answer.

plurality_treatment.quote: Only questions where the answers from both AI trainers were the same were kept in the dataset.
